text: If, in negotiations, you are looked upon as a liar and a trickster, no confidence will be placed in you, nothing will be communicated to you, and you will be in the situation of a man who has been burned in the cheek; and who, from that mark, cannot afterward get an honest livelihood if he would, but must continue a thief.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter C, to his son, London, January 8, Old Style 1750
